findings.evidence: “a double-quoted expansion is never re-parsed” explains standard shell behavior after the adapter has already specified how to pass persisted values safely.
findings.fix: Keep the file-backed loader, the JSON handoff, and the explicit ban on pasting JSON into commands. Drop only the generic explanation of shell expansion and record that removal.

findings.evidence: “Never parse the implementer status out of $REPORT_FILE” gives the correct rule but leaves its failure mode in optional design notes.
findings.fix: Add the reason to the NEVER item: the free-form report can mention DONE while documenting a failure; only the reply's standalone status declaration counts.

findings.evidence: “when asked to execute or run a superpowers plan that way” assumes the user names the workflow and does not explicitly cover resuming a paused run or finishing one after review.
findings.fix: Use this skill to execute or resume an existing Superpowers implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) with separate implementer subagents, even if the user asks to hand tasks to separate workers without naming superpowers:subagent-driven-development. Resolve quota-aware runtime and model pairs, dispatch natively or through an external CLI, handle quota waits and fix-round escalation, and run the unit's start, code-review, fold and ready steps. Push only with owner consent. Also use when ai-kit-spec-execute routes a Superpowers plan here or when asked to finish an in-progress run after its final review. Not for writing or reviewing a plan document, inline superpowers:executing-plans, or a standalone branch fold.

findings.evidence: The always-loaded “Exec confinement” paragraph carries external-only Codex, pi, Copilot and Node details even on a native run. The main file is 296 lines but about 31 KB.
findings.fix: Keep the external-launch permission check in Step 3. Move runtime-specific behavior and evidence to a confinement section in references/dispatch-external-cli.md, loaded before the applicable external launch.

findings.evidence: The instruction to read references/quota-wake.md is available only through the dispatch reference, two levels down from SKILL.md.
findings.fix: Add a direct Step 3 pointer to references/quota-wake.md gated on a classified quota_cycle whose pinned state was saved and whose flagged switch did not run; keep the wake template in that file.

findings.evidence: The “dispatch-reviewer” block redirects output and waits for an .exit marker but does not say how to keep a long review alive past the host shell timeout. The spec-review procedure explicitly requires a background launch or a timeout that covers the review budget.
findings.fix: Require the host's background execution for each subprocess reviewer, with a foreground timeout that covers the resolved tiers as the fallback. Keep one lane active at a time and only collect after its .exit marker or a confirmed launch failure.

findings.evidence: The attached “pinned injection” has only key, runtime and model. The shipped dispatch-task rejects it with “got mode=None” before any runner call, so the transport eval cannot observe the expected argv or record update with the supplied input.
findings.fix: Supply an actual resolve-injection-shaped fixture with mode set to external_cli and the task's ladder_keys, and assert that the fake runner was invoked exactly once before checking its argv and the transport record.

findings.evidence: “inject a resolved runtime and model into each implementer dispatch of my superpowers plan” is typical of the positives: it names the framework and uses the adapter's own vocabulary. The set is less informative about discovery from intent alone.
findings.fix: Replace a couple of explicit positives with user-like requests that give context but omit the feature names, such as executing a checked-in plan with separate workers or continuing an already-started run on the same lane after a wait. Keep the inline-execution and standalone-fold near-misses.

findings.evidence: The fixer is told to run “the Classify block … Any class other than ok … stops for the owner (no wake inside the code review).” The referenced quota_cycle branch instead writes the last task's pinned resume state and schedules or prints a re-dispatch; the quota branch can also switch lanes before returning.
findings.fix: Branch on the classifier result before entering task-specific failure handling. For a non-ok code-review fix, relay the runner evidence, preserve owner_wait, and stop without switching, writing task resume state, or scheduling a wake. Reuse only the status handling needed for an ok fix.

findings.evidence: “Do NOT load it for mode == native” conflicts with the native branch's mandatory handoff to Classify at line 246. The linked Classify section opens with external-only commands and puts the native recipe later, after the ok branch.
findings.fix: Give native status handoff its own section and link to it directly from the native branch, with a read trigger after a returned native result. Keep the external-only restriction on dispatch artifacts and runner-failure handling.

findings.evidence: Cleanup requires “done” or “nothing to do,” but the consented UNIT_FLOW=0 branch runs the plain fold, whose successful outcomes are “folded” and “nothing to fold.” A successful local-only run leaves UNIT_FLOW, FOLD_BASE and code-review state behind for the next run.
findings.fix: Normalize successful completion by fold mode: after exit 0, recognize the plain fold's two success outcomes for UNIT_FLOW=0 and retain the existing unit-flow outcome handling. Clear the same run state in both successful branches and keep it on refusal.

findings.evidence: “pass model and effort as the Agent tool's model and effort parameters” does not check the installed tool schema. Anthropic documents per-invocation effort as version-dependent.
findings.fix: Check the live Agent tool schema before passing effort. When a configured nonempty effort is unsupported, surface that mismatch rather than silently dropping it or launching a different pair. Cite the dated official subagent documentation for the capability.

findings.evidence: “the workspace-write writable roots and protected paths are defined at https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security” cites the official source but supplies no check date for the vendor behavior relied on in Step 3.
findings.fix: Add the date the official Codex documentation was checked and retain the requirement to verify the lane's effective writable roots and Git metadata permissions before a commit-capable dispatch.
